current_example.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.48 <     Z <   1.18).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/f9011a3355b8261e153842a43be45e9bb07240d88421e37f7297a7d0f807e101.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$ 

$$
P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.48<Z<1.18) & =P(Z<1.18)-P(Z\le -0.48) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.18)-P(Z\le -0.48) \\  & =Φ(1.18)-Φ(-0.48)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.48) & =0.3156 \\ Φ(1.18) & =0.8810\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.48<Z<1.18) & =Φ(1.18)-Φ(-0.48) \\  & =0.8810-0.3156 \\  & =0.5654.\end{aligned}
$$
